response.rationale: D5 (Retropharyngeal calcific tendinitis) is strongly supported by the specific findings of "soft-tissue calcification anterior to the C1 arch" and "soft-tissue calcification extending from the longus colli muscle to the atlanto-odontoid joint." These findings directly describe the location and nature of the calcification, which is characteristic of retropharyngeal calcific tendinitis. D2 (Calcific Tendinitis) is a broader category, and while supported by the calcification, D5 is more specific to the described location.
